title: Astrid and the Confession
premise: August Galloway, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made her both brilliant and deliberately invisible, receives a confession letter for a drowning death she investigated years ago—postmarked the day after the victim's funeral. The letter references a ledger of payoffs hidden in plain sight among her own case files, implicating a coastal town's most respected families in a staged accident meant to silence a whistleblower. As August decodes the ledger, she realizes the confession was sent to her because she was there that night, though her memory of it has been carefully buried by trauma and, perhaps, by someone who knew exactly how her mind works. The trail ends at the tide line where the body was found, forcing August to choose between handing the evidence to a compromised justice system or exposing it herself—at the cost of the anonymity that has kept her alive.
about_author: Ulyana Eastwick is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent a decade investigating coastal accidents before turning to fiction. She writes from a house on stilts above a tidal marsh, where the water gives up its secrets twice a day.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: POV: August. Three days after a stranger's funeral, August receives a handwritten confession naming her as witness to a drowning she closed five years ago. Her photographic memory should make the letter trivial to verify—but the handwriting matches no one in her files, including the dead man. Emotional beat: the first crack in her armor of invisibility.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV: August. Reopening her old case file, August notices anomalies only she could see: claim numbers that form a sequence, initials in margin notes spelling out names of the town's founding families. Someone encoded a payoff ledger into official paperwork—and she notarized it without knowing. Emotional beat: dread curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: August, with an interlude from the dead man's widow, Maren. August travels to the coastal town of Bracken Hollow and finds Maren burning correspondence, convinced the confession is a cruel hoax. But Maren lets slip one detail never made public—the victim was wearing someone else's coat. Emotional beat: grief meeting suspicion.

chapters.title: A Memory With Teeth
chapters.summary: POV: August. August interrogates her own recall, reconstructing the night of the death image by image—until she hits a gap, a deliberate blank where her memory should be seamless. Photographs prove she was on the pier that night; her mind has been edited, or she edited it herself. Emotional beat: terror of one's own interior.

chapters.title: The Adjuster's Handshake
chapters.summary: POV: August. A charming senior claims director, Corliss Vane, arrives uninvited, offering August a promotion and gently suggesting she drop the letter as a crank's fantasy. His cufflinks match a monogram in the ledger. He knows about the gap in her memory—and implies he helped create it. Emotional beat: seduction as threat.

chapters.title: Salt and Paper
chapters.summary: POV: Maren. Maren, unable to sleep, rereads her husband's last letters and finds the same numeric sequences August found—he suspected the payoffs and was documenting them. She contacts August, and the two women form an uneasy alliance over coffee and shared guilt. Emotional beat: two kinds of survivor recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Nine Names, One Blank
chapters.summary: POV: August. Decoding completes: nine names took hush money after the whistleblower's 'accident,' and the tenth entry—the payer—is redacted with the same deliberate pattern as August's memory gap. The confession letter's handwriting finally matches: it's her own. Emotional beat: vertigo; the investigator becomes the suspect.

chapters.title: The Night I Don't Remember
chapters.summary: POV: August, fractured across present and recovered fragments. Under hypnosis prompted by Maren, August recovers the pier: she witnessed the staging of the accident, was caught, and traded her testimony for erasure—her own written confession held as leverage ever since. The letter was mailed by whoever now holds it. Emotional beat: shame and self-betrayal laid bare.

chapters.title: Where the Water Gives Up
chapters.summary: POV: August and Corliss, alternating. At low tide, August retrieves the physical ledger from a boathouse cache the victim hid, while Corliss closes in to burn it and her with it. Confrontation on the mudflats turns violent; Maren's arrival tips the balance, and Corliss flees into the channel he once falsified reports about. Emotional beat: the price of survival comes due.

chapters.title: A Confession of My Own
chapters.summary: POV: August. Rather than feed the evidence to Vane's compromised company or a bought town council, August publishes the decoded ledger and her own role in the cover-up, surrendering her license and her invisibility in a single act. Justice arrives outside the law—indictments follow anyway. Standing at the tide line, she finally remembers everything and forgives none of it, least of all herself. Emotional beat: costly, unsentimental peace.
